recommendation: Keep this no-change audit commit as-is. No current FHIR-core source fix is needed for FHIR-16343 unless a future work-group decision changes the broader media-type registration or charset policy.
issue_request: FHIR-16343 was a Published/Persuasive FHIR-core HTTP page correction for STU3. It asked to remove or fix the statement that the HTTP specification defined a default ISO-8859-1 character encoding because that rule did not apply to application/fhir media types and had been removed from later HTTP specifications.
initial_application: Git-svn commit eaa7a5f5e9ab41d2c4a9088649e5dc1f2f8e9f23, matching Jira's svn revision 14172 comment, removed the old source/http.html paragraph that required explicit UTF-8 charset because of an HTTP ISO-8859-1 default and replaced it with optional charset guidance.
additional_context: A 2018 Zulip implementers thread records the same RFC 2616/RFC 7231 rationale from Luis Maas. Earlier FHIR-3777 raised a broader UTF-8/API-page concern but was Resolved - No Change. Later Published FHIR-35811 refined the replacement sentence to avoid implying that application/fhir is itself a valid MIME type.
reconciliation: No source change was made. Current source/http.html says UTF-8 encoding SHALL be used for FHIR instances and may be specified as a MIME type parameter, but is not required; source/xml.html and source/json.html remain consistent about UTF-8.

related_jiras.note: Earlier Resolved - No Change issue on the same HTTP UTF-8/API-page concern; FHIR-16343 later supplied the narrower applied correction.
Later Published issue refined the FHIR-16343 replacement text so it refers to FHIR instances instead of the invalid generic MIME type application/fhir.
